# Independent review - PR 592 @ d18e4e7674c2366324e5e5265e5ceee485737934

## Summary
The three-file diff integrates the already established Lean code-line delta and title formatter into each accepted train member merge. The measurement compares the committed merge tree with its immediate first parent; dropped members cannot contribute to subsequent counts. I found no concrete regression in the title integration.

## Findings
<!-- findings:begin -->
- none
<!-- findings:end -->

## Review
- `local/bin/pr_train.py:90-105` keeps gated titles transient; member records and the publication manifest retain their prior fields. `integrate` measures after the merge commit, then amends only its subject and verifies both parents (`:108-141`). The next iteration uses the amended commit as its baseline.
- `pr_merge.lean_line_delta` counts changed Lean code lines from the compared trees and returns `None` on measurement failure; `merge_commit_title` preserves `[lean 0]`, collapses and sanitizes untrusted titles, and neutralizes issue-closing references. An unavailable count leaves the train's original subject in place. The diff does not change either helper.
- Six focused offline tests passed in 27.072 seconds, including incremental counts, a conflicting dropped member, zero and unavailable deltas, merge parents, shared claims, and pre/post-push member movement. The title fixture retains a newer main-only Lean file without counting it as a deletion. The existing manifest, checked transport and post-push checks are unchanged.
- The commit and PR use the expected issue, title and body conventions. The EVOLUTION entry records the owner decision and accurately describes the new code path. The published input reports all nine exact-head local CI contexts green, and the author records 729 workflow tests (9 skipped) and a rooted audit of 1,659 passes, zero failures and three existing warnings.

## Verification limits
- No live train, full hook suite, Lake build or CI rerun was performed in this independent review. CI and author test counts above are publication evidence, not tests personally rerun here. The existing issue #507 transport contract is accepted and was not reopened.

VERDICT: APPROVED

pr.body:
### Motivation
- Address #590: every first-parent merge on main should carry the owner's Lean line delta, including members of the reviewed merge train. Ordinary merges already use the policy implemented by #558 for #557.

### Description
- Measure each accepted member's actual merged result against the immediately preceding accepted train commit and reuse the existing delta and title formatter.
- Preserve zero and unavailable-measurement behavior, title sanitization, member heads, merge topology, manifest format, claims and transport checks.
- Add Git fixtures for sequential increments, unrelated newer-main Lean content, conflicts, zero deltas, sanitization and unavailable measurements; record the policy integration in EVOLUTION.

### Testing
- Published head `d18e4e7674c2366324e5e5265e5ceee485737934`: all nine local CI statuses passed in 421 seconds. All eight gates ran, including build, blueprint rendering, synchronization and statement-origin.
- The CI workflow suite passed 729 tests with 9 skipped. Normal commit hooks also passed 729 tests with 9 skipped; the focused train suite passed 26 tests, and the additional unavailable-measurement fixture passed.
- The rooted axiom audit passed 1,659 declarations with zero failures and three existing statement-level warnings. Syntax, whitespace, hook setup and all four author artifact hashes were verified.
- Git-backed fixtures exercised member subjects and transport behavior; no live train has run.

---
Addresses #590
